Exercise A

Plan the project

Breakout rooms, 30 minutes, groups of three. The Facilities Manager approved your meeting on Tuesday. Now your team needs a plan. There is not enough time or money for all eight milestones: sort them, plan the timeline, and cut two. Then everyone types the group’s plan.

The brief: Quiet Library pilot

Goal: make the second-floor reading room of the library quiet enough to study in before the January exams.

Dates: 1 December – 31 January. The campus is closed from 18 December to 11 January. Your team has exams from 25 January.

Resources: a budget of €1,500 and about 20 working days for the whole team.

Stakeholders: the Facilities Manager (approves spending and wants a final report by 31 January), the library staff (worried about extra work) and the students who use the room.

The eight milestones

M1 Survey 200 students about noise · 5 days · €0
M2 Agree quiet-zone rules with the library staff · 2 days · €0
M3 Put up signs and floor markings · 3 days · €400
M4 Build two phone booths for calls · 10 days · €1,200
M5 Train 10 student volunteers as quiet monitors · 4 days · €150
M6 Launch event with free coffee · 2 days · €300
M7 Measure noise levels before and after · 3 days · €0
M8 Write the final report for the Facilities Manager · 4 days · €0

All eight: 33 days and €2,050.

Step 1 · MoSCoW: sort the milestones

Must: the pilot fails without it. Should: important, but it can wait. Could: nice if there is time. Won’t: not in this project. Two milestones must be Won’t.

Exercise B

Talking about progress

On your own, 10 minutes. Read each sentence to the end, then choose the word or form that fits. The last gap revises an earlier week.

Exercise C

Status update

On your own, 15 minutes. First write the term for each definition: there is no word bank. Then write your group’s status update to the Facilities Manager.

Key terms: write the word
Word count: 0

Say what will have been done by 17 December, what the team will be doing in January, which two milestones you cut and why, and ask for one thing. Use at least three of these terms: milestone, deliverable, stakeholder, delegate, on track.
